permutationLabel: Very elderly, rivaroxaban, heart failure — pre-endoscopy Rockall 5
summary: 84-year-old man with heart failure and AF on rivaroxaban; melaena, HR 106, SBP 108, Hb 10.4, urea 16.2 (GBS 12; pre-endoscopy Rockall 5: age ≥80 → 2, pulse >100 → 1, heart failure → 2).

inputs.hpi: Daughter reports three days of black tarry stools and increasing tiredness. Known heart failure and atrial fibrillation on rivaroxaban. Mild ankle swelling as usual. No haematemesis, no collapse.

exam.general: Frail, pale. Pulse irregular 106/min, BP 108/64. JVP not raised. Mild pitting ankle oedema.

inputs.socialHistory: Lives with daughter. Walks with a stick.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute upper GI bleed on rivaroxaban
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute upper GI bleed (melaena) on rivaroxaban, heart failure. Glasgow-Blatchford 12, pre-endoscopy Rockall 5.

recommended.note: NICE CG141 uses the pre-endoscopy (admission) Rockall score as well as the Blatchford score.

mustInclude.note: DOAC clearance depends on renal function.
Heart failure is cardiovascular disease: threshold 8 g/dL.
mustInclude.proposedFix: upper_gi_bleed protocol: add the ESGE cardiovascular threshold (Hb ≤8 g/dL, target ≥10) and key it on cardiac comorbidity.

mustExclude.proposedFix: Remove tranexamic acid from the upper_gi_bleed protocol medications (ESGE 2021 recommends against it; HALT-IT). Surgeon sign-off needed.

guideline.name: ESGE Guideline — endoscopic diagnosis and management of nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage (NVUGIH), update 2021
guideline.section: DOACs: withhold at presentation; reversal agents/PCC only for life-threatening bleeding; transfusion threshold ≤8 g/dL with cardiovascular disease
guideline.citation: Gralnek IM, Stanley AJ, Morris AJ, et al. Endoscopy. 2021;53:300–332.

guideline.name: NICE CG141 — Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in over 16s: management
guideline.section: Formal risk assessment with Blatchford at first assessment and full Rockall after endoscopy
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG141. London: NICE; 2012 (last updated 2016).

guideline.name: Rockall score — derivation
guideline.section: Pre-endoscopy components: age (≥80 → 2), shock (pulse >100 → 1; SBP <100 → 2), comorbidity (cardiac failure/IHD → 2; renal/liver failure, disseminated malignancy → 3)
guideline.citation: Rockall TA, Logan RF, Devlin HB, Northfield TC. Risk assessment after acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Gut. 1996;38:316–321.

guideline.name: Glasgow-Blatchford score — derivation
guideline.citation: Blatchford O, Murray WR, Blatchford M. A risk score to predict need for treatment for upper-gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Lancet. 2000;356:1318–1321.

guideline.name: BSG-led multisociety consensus care bundle — early clinical management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Care bundle: group and save; review anticoagulants
guideline.citation: Siau K, Hearnshaw S, Stanley AJ, et al. Frontline Gastroenterol. 2020;11:311–323.

guideline.name: HALT-IT randomised trial — tranexamic acid in gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Tranexamic acid: no benefit, more venous thromboembolism
guideline.citation: HALT-IT Trial Collaborators. Effects of a high-dose 24-h infusion of tranexamic acid on death and thromboembolic events in patients with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (HALT-IT). Lancet. 2020;395:1927–1936.

rationale: Elderly/anticoagulated permutation: very old age, heart failure, CKD and a DOAC. Tests the Rockall suggestion, the DOAC flag, renal function for DOAC clearance, the cardiovascular transfusion threshold and absence of heparin bridging.

authoring.author: Claude (upper-GI cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations written from the guideline texts, not yet checked against the source (verified: false).
